subject: parameter-binding order and parameter-set resolution
statement: **Parameter binding order and parameter-set resolution (CF-BND-001).** Command-line binding runs these steps in order: (1) arguments that came from hashtable splatting are moved after all other arguments; (2) a parameter name with no value is joined with the next argument as its value (a switch parameter takes `$true` instead; a name followed by another recognizable parameter name, or a name at the end, is a `MissingArgument` error); (3) **named binding**: every argument with a name is matched (exact name or alias first, then unambiguous prefix); a parameter already bound is an error (`ParameterAlreadyBound`) except that a splatted entry whose name was already bound explicitly is skipped; the `--%` verbatim marker is consumed here; (4) **positional binding**: unbound parameters that have a position in the still-valid sets are grouped by position number in ascending order; arguments without a name are taken in order; each is offered to the parameters of that position in four attempts — default set without type coercion, all valid sets without coercion, default set with coercion, all valid sets with coercion — and an argument no parameter accepts stays unbound; (5) values from `$PSDefaultParameterValues` are bound to still-unbound parameters, after positional binding and again after dynamic parameters; (6) `ValidateParameterSets`; (7) dynamic parameters are fetched once from the command (`GetDynamicParameters`), merged into the parameter table and set bitmasks, and named and positional binding are repeated for the leftover arguments; (8) leftover arguments are bound to the single `ValueFromRemainingArguments` parameter (two such parameters in the current sets is an error); (9) any argument still unbound is an error (`NamedParameterNotFound` for a named one, `PositionalParameterNotFound` otherwise); (10) the final parameter-set check and the mandatory-parameter step (§7); (11) script parameters that are still unbound get their declared default values; (12) the set mask is saved for pipeline binding. **Parameter-set resolution:** each bound parameter narrows the current set mask to the sets it belongs to. After binding, with *one* valid set that set is chosen. With *several* valid sets: if the mask is "all sets" and the command has no default set, the call is accepted as set-less; else if the command defines a default set and it is among the valid sets, the command's parameter-set name is set to the default set, and the mask is narrowed to the default set only in validation calls that ask for it (the final check after command-line binding does; the checks made before dynamic parameters and during pipeline binding may not); else, if pipeline input is still expected and some valid set has an unbound parameter that takes pipeline input, the decision is postponed to pipeline binding; else the mask is reduced to sets with no unbound mandatory parameter; if exactly one set remains it is chosen, otherwise `AmbiguousParameterSet`. With *zero* valid sets (conflicting parameters) the result is `AmbiguousParameterSet` as well. **Pipeline-object binding** for each input object restores the saved mask and the original values of parameters bound by the previous object, then makes four passes over the unbound parameters that accept pipeline input — (a) by value without coercion, (b) by property name without coercion, (c) by value with coercion, (d) by property name with coercion — trying the default set before the other valid sets in each pass; a successful bind narrows the set mask again.
label: FACT-SRC

subject: compile-versus-interpret decision rule
statement: **Compile-versus-interpret rule.** Every named block is turned into one expression-tree lambda. At creation of the delegate (`Compiler.CompileTree`), the tiering mode is `NeverCompile` if the script block's total statement count (`_stmtCount`) is greater than 300, otherwise `CompileOnDemand`; `AlwaysCompile` exists but no caller passes it. The delegate starts as an **interpreted** `LightLambda` with a call counter of 32 (`CompileOnDemand`, threshold -1 mapped to `DefaultCompilationThreshold`) or `int.MaxValue` (`NeverCompile`). Each call decrements the counter; the call that reads 0 (the 33rd) queues JIT compilation of the whole lambda on a thread-pool thread and is itself still interpreted; once the compiled delegate exists, every later call uses it. A lambda is **never interpreted** (JIT-compiled at once, synchronously) when the light compiler meets a method call with a by-ref parameter, an instance call on a non-primitive value type, or a constructor with a by-ref parameter; and trap-handler lambdas and single-expression lambdas are always built with `LambdaExpression.Compile()` (never interpreted). Loops are promoted separately (CF-CMP-002).
label: FACT-SRC

subject: every threshold and limit of the tiering policy
statement: **Tiering thresholds and limits.** Statement count above which a script block is never JIT-compiled by call count: 300 (`_stmtCount > 300`, `Compiler.Compile`). Interpreted calls before JIT: 32 (`LightCompiler.DefaultCompilationThreshold`), so JIT starts on the 33rd call; `int.MaxValue` for `NeverCompile`; threshold 0 or 1 means synchronous compilation (never produced by `Compiler`). Loop iterations before loop JIT: 16 (constructor argument of `EnterLoopInstruction` in `EnterLoopExpression.AddInstructions`), so the loop JIT starts on the 17th arrival at the loop top. Loop statement count at or above which a loop is never promoted: 300 (`LoopStatementCount < 300` required to emit the loop counter). Maximum delegate parameters of an interpreted lambda: 16 (`LightLambda.MaxParameters`). Compile helper cache of delegate `Run` factories: 100 entries (`CacheDict` in `LightLambda`). Parsed-script cache (shares compiled delegates between clones): cleared completely when it holds more than 1024 entries (`ScriptBlock.CacheScriptBlock`).
label: FACT-SRC

subject: optimized-versus-unoptimized preconditions
statement: **Optimized versus unoptimized.** A script block clause is run from the optimized code (variables in fixed tuple slots) only if the engine is not debugging (`ExecutionContext._debuggingMode <= 0`) **and** the invocation creates a new local scope (`createLocalScope`, i.e. not dot-sourced); the same two conditions are used by the command processors that run script blocks (`DlrScriptCommandProcessor` constructor) and script cmdlets. If the optimized compile shows that any slot-allocated variable name could be an `AllScope` variable (`VariableAnalysis.AnyVariablesCouldBeAllScope`), the unoptimized variant is used instead, and both variants are compiled. In the unoptimized variant only the automatic variables (plus the preference variables for script cmdlets) get tuple slots and every other variable is looked up by name. Independently of this choice, variable analysis allocates no slots for a block that uses `New-Variable`, `Remove-Variable`, `Set-Variable`, `Set-PSBreakpoint` (or their aliases), dot-sourcing or `$private:` variables.
label: FACT-SRC

subject: conversion algorithm and converter order
statement: **Conversion algorithm and converter order.** For a source type S and target type T the engine returns the first applicable converter in this order (cached per type pair): (1) a cached entry; (2) if S is the null type: `Nullable<…>` → null, any reference type → null, a value type → no conversion (numeric, `char`, `string`, `bool`, `PSReference`, `switch` and `void` targets have pre-cached null conversions); (3) if T is assignable from S: identity (same type) or assignable; (4) by-ref-like types: none; (5) S is a `PSObject`: none (the caller unwraps first); (6) T is `PSObject`: wrap; (7) under Constrained Language Mode: only targets `object`, `object[]` or the core type list are converted (others are refused, or only audited in WDAC audit mode); (8) **language conversions**: `Nullable<U>` through U, `void`, `bool` (from `IList`, enum, value type, class), `string`, arrays (related arrays element-wise, unrelated arrays per element, enumerable to array, scalar to one-element array), `Array`, `Hashtable` from `IDictionary`, `PSReference`, `XmlDocument`, `StringCollection`, `ScriptBlock` to delegate, `PSCustomObject`, integer to enum, `PSMethod` to delegate; (9) a static `Parse` method on T; (10) a static `Create` method; (11) a constructor of T taking S; (12) a cast operator (implicit, then explicit) on S or T; (13) `IConvertible` (numeric sources through the string-convertible path, other `IConvertible` sources via `Convert`); (14) for an `IDictionary` source: T's no-argument constructor then property assignment from the keys; (15) an `IEnumerable` constructor; (16) property-based conversion; if S or T may have a `TypeConverter`/`PSTypeConverter`, or a value-dependent converter was found, the result is wrapped to try the custom/value-dependent converter first and the found converter second; (17) otherwise no conversion (rank `None`, a failing converter that raises `PSInvalidCastException`). Numeric-to-numeric, number-to-string, number-to-bool and null-to-number conversions are pre-cached with fixed ranks.
label: FACT-SRC

subject: command resolution order
statement: **Command resolution order (CF-DSC-001).** For one name the searcher tries, in this order and returning the first match that is allowed: (1) **alias** (a match whose visibility does not allow the caller's origin is skipped and the search continues with functions); (2) **function / filter / configuration**; (3) **cmdlet** (a module-qualified name `Module\Cmdlet` matches only cmdlets of that module; with several cmdlets of the same name in different modules, the first in table order is returned unless all scopes are searched); (4) if application or external-script types are allowed: a name that is a *qualified provider path* is resolved as a path; then an absolute path to an existing file; then the file system search of each `PATH` directory in order (for a name with a directory part: only that directory); then a PowerShell-relative path (name starting with `.`, `~` or `\`). Within one directory the candidate file names are, in order: the name itself first if it already has an extension; `name.ps1` when external scripts are allowed (also `.psm1` and `.psd1` in non-discovery searches); on Windows every `PATHEXT` extension when applications are allowed; then the bare name if not yet added. A `.ps1` file becomes an external script; any other existing file becomes an application. If the normal search fails and the name contains neither `-` nor `\`, the lookup is repeated once with the name prefixed with `Get-`. If still unresolved, module-qualified names trigger module auto-loading, and (with `$PSModuleAutoLoadingPreference` = `All`, the default) other names trigger module auto-discovery against the module analysis cache; then the *command-not-found* handler runs; then a `CommandNotFoundException` is raised. In a session whose origin is `Runspace`, application and external-script types are removed from the search when the session state has no allowed applications or scripts, and a name with a directory part must match an allow-list entry (prefix match, or the list is exactly `*`).
label: FACT-SRC

subject: terminating/non-terminating errors; try/catch/finally/trap ordering
statement: **Terminating versus non-terminating errors; try/catch/finally/trap ordering (CF-ERR-001).** (1) A *non-terminating* error is an `ErrorRecord` written to the error stream by a command (`WriteError`); it does not interrupt the command or the pipeline, sets the pipeline's failed state and `$?` to false, and is subject to the command's `ErrorAction` (`Ignore`: dropped, not recorded; `SilentlyContinue`: recorded in `$Error`/`-ErrorVariable` but not shown; `Continue`: recorded and written; `Inquire`: ask, then as `Continue` or stop; `Stop`: converted to a terminating `ActionPreferenceStopException`). (2) A *terminating* error is an exception: `ThrowTerminatingError` from a cmdlet (wrapped as `CmdletInvocationException`), `throw`, a runtime error in an expression, or `ActionPreferenceStop`. It stops the current *statement* and, unless handled, the command, and is recorded as the pipeline's first terminating error (later ones are only logged). (3) In **script code every statement is guarded**: when a statement throws a non-flow-control exception the engine consults `$ErrorActionPreference` (default `Continue`): `SilentlyContinue`/`Ignore` resume with the next statement; `Continue` reports the error record and resumes with the next statement — except that an exception produced by a `throw` statement is rethrown when no trap is present; `Stop` rethrows (terminates the enclosing scope and propagates); `Inquire` prompts. (4) **Handler order** for one thrown exception: innermost enclosing `try` is searched first; its `catch` clauses are tried in source order with the first matching type winning (a catch without a type matches any `RuntimeException`; `PipelineStoppedException` is never caught by a type-less catch); `finally` runs after the try/catch block completes, on normal exit, after a caught exception, and while an unhandled exception propagates; if no `catch` in the `try` matches, the exception propagates to the enclosing `try`, then to `trap` handlers of the enclosing blocks (a trap matches by the exception type, trying the inner exception before the outer one), then to the statement-level preference rule of (3). A `trap` runs in a new scope with `$_` set to the error record; `continue` in a trap means *SilentlyContinue*, `break` means *Stop*; otherwise the action is the current preference. (5) Flow control (`break`, `continue`, `return`, `exit`) travels as exceptions that are never caught by `catch` or traps and are rethrown by the statement guard. (6) `$?` is true after a statement that completes without error and false after a statement in which an error (terminating-handled or non-terminating) occurred; the pipeline-level failed state also covers errors written by commands.
label: FACT-SRC

subject: parse-error limits and recovery rule
statement: **Parse-error limits and recovery rule.** The parser never throws for a syntax error: each error is appended to `Parser.ErrorList` after de-duplication (an error is dropped only if an earlier error has the same ID and the same start and end line and column), there is no limit on the number of errors, and parsing continues by returning partial or error nodes (`ErrorStatementAst`, `ErrorExpressionAst`), by pretending a missing closing token was present, or by skipping tokens to a synchronization token (`SyncOnError`, which tracks nesting of `()`, `{}` and `[]` and never consumes end of input); `ParseError.IncompleteInput` is true only when the error was reported with `ReportIncompleteInput` and the error position is at the end of the script apart from whitespace and comments. The only exceptions are an exhausted execution stack (the whole parse is retried once on a new thread, then `ScriptTooComplicated` is reported) and any other exception during `ParseFile`/`ParseInput`, which is wrapped as a `ParseException` with `UnrecoverableParserError`.
label: FACT-SRC

subject: member resolution order
statement: **Member resolution order (CF-ETS-001).** Looking up member *name* on a value `v` (wrapped as a `PSObject`) proceeds in this order and returns the first hit: (1) the reserved names `psbase`, `psadapted`, `psextended`, `psobject` and `pstypenames`, generated on demand; (2) **instance members** added to this object (for example by `Add-Member`); (3) **type-table (extended) members** merged over the object's type-name hierarchy, most specific type name winning; (4) **adapted members** from the adapter chosen for the object; (5) **base members**: the .NET members of the wrapped object, only when the chosen adapter is not already the .NET adapter. Member-name matching in the .NET adapter is case-insensitive (its binding flags include `IgnoreCase`). Type-table collection entries are marked "replicate and clone when returning" (a copy bound to the current object is handed out), adapted and base entries are not; the enumeration order across sources is `UNVERIFIED` (VB-038). Member lookup on a `PSMemberSet` owner searches the set's own members first, then the same collections.
label: FACT-SRC

subject: statement, pipeline and command grammar; statement terminators
statement: **Statement and terminator rule.** A statement list is parsed as: skip any run of newlines and semicolons; parse a statement; skip any run of newlines and semicolons; stop when the next token is `)` or `}` or no statement can be parsed. A terminator is **not** required between statements that end with a closing `}` (e.g. `if`, loops, `try`, `function`), because the list only skips optional terminators; a pipeline (or any statement parsed by `PipelineChainRule`) ends at newline, `;`, `)`, `}`, `&&`/`||` (chain), `&` (background) or end of input, and any other token after a complete pipeline element is `UnexpectedToken`. Newlines continue a construct only in these places: after `|`, before a `|` that starts the next line, after `&&` and `||`, after each binary or unary operator and after `,`, after `=` in an assignment, inside `( )`, after `?`/`:` of a ternary, between `}` and `elseif`/`else`/`catch`/`finally`, and after a backtick line continuation handled by the tokenizer.
label: FACT-SRC

subject: command and script lifecycle (begin/process/end/clean, cmdlet lifecycle)
statement: **Command lifecycle (CF-LCY-001).** For a pipeline of commands C1…Cn the engine (1) builds all command processors and wires pipes; (2) *prepares* every command in order (parameter binding from the command line, with default parameter values applied) and sets up common-parameter variables; (3) runs the *begin* phase of every command in order C1…Cn (`BeginProcessing`, or the `begin` block); (4) runs the *process* phase *depth-first and synchronously*: C1 reads its input (or runs once with no input if none is expected), and each object it writes into its output pipe causes C2 to run its process phase over everything queued (the default buffer threshold is zero), recursively; every input object is bound before each call (pipeline parameter binding, then mandatory-parameter check); an object that cannot be bound or misses a mandatory parameter produces a non-terminating error and is skipped; (5) when C1's input is exhausted the *end* phase runs for C1…Cn in order — each command first drains any input still queued through its process phase, then runs `EndProcessing` (or the `end` block); (6) the *clean* phase (`clean` blocks, only for commands that have one) runs for every command in `finally`, with stopping suspended, and its errors are written to the command's error output; (7) all command processors are disposed. The first terminating error is recorded; later failures are logged as health events and do not replace it. A stop request cancels the pipeline token and calls `StopProcessing` on every command.
label: FACT-SRC

subject: tokenizer mode switching rule (command vs expression mode, when it switches)
statement: **Mode rule.** The tokenizer starts in Command mode; the parser switches to Expression mode when it parses an expression operand/operator position (including the first element of a pipeline when it is not a command), to Command mode when it parses a command's arguments or the body of `{ }`, `( )`, `$( )`, to TypeName mode inside `[...]` type literals, and to Signature mode for class/enum/method headers; every switch is restored in a `finally` block, and a switch discards and rescans a pending lookahead token unless its kind is `ParseModeInvariant`.
label: FACT-SRC

subject: numeric-literal rules (radix, suffixes, multipliers)
statement: **Numeric literal rules.** A number is an optional sign (`-`, en/em dash/horizontal bar, or `+`; only when `AllowSignedNumbers`), then either `.digits[exponent]`, `0x` hex digits, `0b` binary digits, or decimal digits with optional `.digits` and `e/E[+|-]digits`; then an optional type suffix (`u s l d y n`, plus a second character only after `u`: `ul us uy`), then an optional multiplier `k m g t p` that **must be followed by `b`/`B`** (powers of 1024; the suffix comes before the multiplier); the literal must be followed by a token terminator (in Expression mode also by a binary-operator start character) or the text is not a number and is rescanned as a generic token. Value typing: no suffix → `int`, else `long`, else (decimal format only) `decimal`, else `double`; real literals → `double` unless suffix `d` (`decimal`); hex and binary are two's complement with the sign decided by the top digit (`0xFFFFFFFF` → `-1`, `0xFF` → `255`), a 16-hex-digit or 64-bit-digit literal without `u` becomes `long`; the multiplier is applied to the value before the range cast and failure to fit returns `false` (reported as `BadNumericConstant` in Expression mode, otherwise the text becomes a generic token).
label: FACT-SRC

subject: module load, export and auto-load rules
statement: **Module load, export and auto-load rules (CF-MOD-001).** (1) A module name without a path is searched in each `PSModulePath` entry in order (entries marked to skip the system folder are skipped; on Unix the folder name is matched case-insensitively): in an entry, the module base is `<entry>/<name>`; its version sub-folders are tried first (the first whose version satisfies the constraints and equals its manifest's `ModuleVersion` is loaded); if none loads, the files `<entry>/<name>/<name>` + extension are tried in the order `.psd1`, `.psm1`, `.cdxml`, `.ni.dll`, `.dll`, `.exe` (a name that already carries a module extension is tried as given); the first successful load ends the search and its exports are added to the analysis cache. (2) A manifest is read as data and its keys are checked against the known key list (§4); the processing of the root module, nested modules, required modules (version-constrained; a cyclic-requirement check exists), required assemblies, scripts to process, types and formats follows, in an order that is `UNVERIFIED` (VB-046); how the manifest export lists combine with a script module's own exports is `UNVERIFIED` (VB-046). (3) A module already loaded that satisfies the requested constraints is not loaded again unless `-Force`; only its members are re-imported with the requested prefix and options. (4) Each module has its own session state; exported commands are copied into the importer's session state. (5) `Export-ModuleMember` selects exports by wildcard patterns per category (functions, cmdlets, variables, aliases), skipping `AllScope` items and built-in variable names. (6) Import applies `-Prefix`/`DefaultCommandPrefix`, `-NoClobber`, visibility and the verb/noun checks, in that order: cmdlets, aliases, functions, variables. (7) **Auto-loading** happens during command lookup: a module-qualified name loads exactly that module; any other unknown command name is looked up in the analysis cache of every module file on `PSModulePath` and the first module exporting a command of that exact name is imported (`$PSModuleAutoLoadingPreference`: `None`, `ModuleQualified`, `All`). (8) Removal of a module (`RemoveModule`) is `UNVERIFIED` here (VB-046).
label: FACT-SRC

subject: operator precedence and associativity
statement: **Operator precedence and associativity.** Binary operators are parsed by precedence climbing and **all are left-associative**; from lowest to highest precedence the levels are: logical (`-and`, `-or`, `-xor`) = 1; bitwise (`-band`, `-bor`, `-bxor`) = 2; comparison group (all `-eq`/`-ne`/`-gt`/`-ge`/`-lt`/`-le`, `-like`, `-match`, `-replace`, `-contains`, `-in` families with their `i`/`c` variants, `-is`, `-isnot`, `-as`, `-split`, `-join`, `-shl`, `-shr`) = 5; null-coalescing `??` = 7; additive (`+`, `-`) = 9; multiplicative (`*`, `/`, `%`) = 10; format `-f` = 12; range `..` = 13. The comma (array-literal) operator binds tighter than every binary operator; the unary operators, casts and `++`/`--` bind tighter than the comma; the ternary `?:` (right-nested) and assignment (`=`, `+=`, `-=`, `*=`, `/=`, `%=`, `??=`, parsed at statement level with a statement on the right) bind looser than all binary operators; `&&` and `||` chain pipelines and are not expression operators. Operators spelled with a leading dash are recognized as operators only when the tokenizer is in expression mode.
label: FACT-SRC

subject: output unrolling and enumeration rules
statement: **Output unrolling and enumeration rules.** A value is *enumerated* (treated as a sequence) when, after unwrapping `PSObject`: it is `AutomationNull` (empty sequence), an array, a `DataTable` (its rows), a COM enumerable, any other `IEnumerable` that is not a string, `IDictionary` or `XmlNode` (the generic `IEnumerable<T>` enumerator is preferred), or an `IEnumerator`; `null`, strings, dictionaries (hashtables), `XmlNode` and all other objects are **not** enumerated and are single values. When a statement writes its value to the output pipe: `AutomationNull` writes nothing; a non-enumerable value is written as one object (mutable value types are copied first); an enumerable value is **unrolled exactly one level**: each element is written separately (elements that are themselves collections stay whole), and an enumerator is disposed afterwards if the engine created it.
label: FACT-SRC

subject: scope, variable lookup and assignment rules
statement: **Scope, lookup and assignment rules.** A variable name is parsed into an optional scope qualifier (`global:`, `local:`, `script:`, `private:`) or a provider drive (`name:`), and an unqualified name. **Reading:** an unqualified name is searched in the current scope and then in each parent scope up to the global scope, and the first match wins; a variable marked `Private` is skipped when it is found in any scope other than the current one; `global:`, `local:`/`private:` and `script:` search exactly one scope (the global scope, the current scope, the script scope respectively); inside one scope the compiled locals tuple (and any dot-sourced tuples) is checked before the variable table; a drive-qualified name is read through the provider. A name that is not found yields `$null`, or a `VariableIsUndefined` error under strict mode (version 2: always; version 1: except inside expandable strings). **Writing:** an unqualified or `local:`/`private:` assignment always targets the current scope (a parent's variable of the same name is never modified; a new local variable is created if the current scope has none), `script:` and `global:` target the script and global scope; assigning to an existing variable in the target scope keeps its object and replaces its value after running its attributes (transformation, then validation), and a `ReadOnly` or `Constant` variable cannot be written (`VariableNotWritable`; `-Force` can overwrite `ReadOnly` but never `Constant`). **New scopes:** every function or script block call (not dot-sourcing) creates a child scope whose parent is the caller's scope; the script scope is the nearest enclosing scope created for a script file, or the global scope; variables marked `AllScope` are shared by reference with every new scope. **Dot-sourcing** creates no scope: the callee's locals tuple is pushed onto the current scope's `DottedScopes` for the duration of the call.
label: FACT-SRC
